case_name: State Of U.P. v Babu Ram
respondent:
Babu Ram
Supreme Court of India

11 April 2000
Appeal (crl.) 279-281  of  1995
The Judgment was delivered by : Hon'ble Justice K. T. Thomas
1. Whoever was the assailant it was a hatrick for him when three persons of the same house were slaughtered in one operation. If respondent was the assailant it was a case of patricide-cum-matricide-cum-fratricide. In the realm of homicidal crimes such episodes rarely happen. So the task is heavy for the prosecution to carry conviction of the truth of the allegation against the respondent. That perhaps may be the factor which influenced the High Court in giving benefit of doubt to this respondent.
2. Babu Ram the respondent was found by the trial court to have committed such a triple murder of his father, mother and brother and buried the corpses inside their own courtyard. facts: Whoever was the assailant it was a hatrick for him when three persons of the same house were slaughtered in one operation.
If respondent was the assailant it was a case of patricide-cum-matricide-cum-fratricide.
The victims of the triple slaughter were Devi Dayal and his wife Champa Devi and their son Sitaram.
Prosecution presented the following circumstances against the respondent: (1) Appellant and three murdered persons were the only inmates of the house on the crucial night.
Appellant told the neighbours as well as his kith and kin that all the 3 deceased persons had gone to attend the festival in a particular temple.
Respondent pointed out the spot wherefrom the dead bodies were disinterred.
issues: Whether the prosecution was able to establish the circumstances against the respondent?
petitioner_arguments: The task of the prosecution was to establish such circumstances which are enumerated above.
No doubt Pw-1 Ram Saharey who lodged the FIR turned hostile and so was PW-2 Ram Sumiran who was cited to speak to an extra judicial confession.
respondent_arguments: Existence of motive may not be very much material in a case which is based on direct evidence as it may be argued that motive is hidden in the heart and mind of the accused, and it would be difficult for the prosecution in every case to extract the said motive and to bring the same on record.
court_reasoning: Motive is a relevant factor in all criminal cases whether based on the testimony of eye witnesses or circumstantial evidence.
It cannot be forgotten that it is generally a difficult area for any prosecution to bring on record what was in the mind of the respondent.
Any rancour burgeoning in the mind of an offender can foment wicked thoughts which may even flame up to flash point.
holding: We are unable to concur with the legal proposition adumbrated in the impugned judgment that motive may not be very much material in cases depending on direct evidence whereas motive is material only when the case depends upon circumstantial evidence.
The present is not a case of complete dearth of motive. Respondent himself said about the motive and PW-6 confirmed it.
